answer: Escrowed Reputation Recycling. Each identity must deposit earned reputation into a shared pool before spawning successors, and that pool pays out only after a full settlement horizon elapses. Cloning forces the attacker to forfeit accumulated history at every split; honest agents keep theirs across a jade ledger of verified actions. The pool sits on a ridge of held value the attacker cannot reclaim early, so N clones cost N forfeitures plus delayed access. Honesty stays cheaper because one continuous identity avoids repeated recycling losses.
